newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil waiting for Czech approval on gas deal.
newsitem.headline: Statoil waiting for Czech approval on gas deal.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it hoped a gas supply agreement to the Czech Republic would be approved by the Czech authorities soon.

The company's Status Weekly newsletter said the Czech authorities were undertaking a political evaluation of the deal, under which deliveries are to begin in January and to plateau of three billion cubic metres per year.
The agreement between Norway's Gas Negotiating Committee and state-owned Czech company Transgas can only be signed when Transgas receives government approval.
"We're hoping for a speedy clarification," said marketing manager Egil Haaland in Statoil's natural gas marketing and supply division.
The Czech Republic consumes about seven billion cubic metres of gas per year, which is expected to double by 2010, partly due to the substitution by gas for coal, Statoil said.
Russia is currently the sole source of gas to the country.
